title: Add KMS-budgeting middleware and residency-aware audit-cohort linker
author: Samir Patel
description:
Context: Customers have asked for stronger controls to limit cross-tenant KMS spend and to correlate KMS usage with residency assertions in audit logs without enlarging the audit surface. This PR implements a lightweight KMS consumption governor middleware plus an audit-cohort linker that attaches residency-provenance tags to KMS and audit events to improve downstream compliance analysis.

Motivation: Two recurring gaps from audits: (1) lack of per-operator/tenant runtime throttles for KMS operations which causes noisy billing spikes during misbehaving jobs, and (2) difficulty tracing which residency decision (region assertion) led to a particular KMS wrap/unwrap event in the audit index. Existing solutions either required heavy policy changes or duplicated audit payloads. This change aims to be minimal-risk, opt-in via config, and compatible with RBAC v2 assertions.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds a KMS budgeting middleware that tracks short-window consumption of KMS primitives (Encrypt/Decrypt/Sign/Verify/WrapKey) per-operator and per-tenant. The governor enforces soft limits (rate advisory) and hard limits (reject with 429) configurable via cluster policy and per-tenant overrides.
- Introduces a residency-aware audit-cohort linker that emits a compact provenance token (cohort_id) derived from the residency assertion used during request evaluation and attaches it to KMS audit entries and retention profiles. Cohort IDs are one-way hashes (salted by cluster key) to avoid leaking explicit region tags in logs while enabling correlation.
- Extends RBAC v2 decision path to surface the originating residency assertion id to the request context so middleware can link it to KMS usage without altering PDP policy syntax.
- Adds migration tooling: a small compatibility shim that backfills cohort_id for recent KMS events (90-day window) using recorded residency decisions when available. Backfill is rate-limited and runs as a separate job.

Design notes: The governor uses a token-bucket per (tenant_id, operator_id, kms_primitive) keyed store with local in-memory fast-path and periodic coordinator for global limits. Hard limits only apply when a tenant global override is set to deny burst; otherwise we emit advisory metrics and tag traces for throttling suggestions. Cohort linking intentionally stores only hashed tokens and a minimal mapping table for historical backfill; keys are rotated monthly.

Backwards compatibility and opt-in: All behavior is disabled by default. Cluster admins can opt-in via redwood-config.kms.governor.enabled=true and toggle per-tenant profiles. RBAC decisions remain unchanged; we only expose the residency assertion id via a new context header (internal only) used by middleware and the backfill worker.

Checklist:
- [x] KMS governor core implementation + unit tests
- [x] Audit-cohort linker + integration tests in local harness
- [x] RBAC v2 decision context plumbing and feature flag
- [x] Backfill worker + migration docs
- [x] Docs/console UI config exposure (defaults hidden behind feature flag)
- [x] E2E smoke in staging with synthetic load

Rollout plan: Deploy feature-gated on staging for one week with advisory-only mode (no hard rejects). If metrics look stable, enable hard-limit mode for a small canary tenant group, monitor billing deltas and KMS error spikes, then enable global opt-in. Backfill job will be scheduled post-canary.

Related: ENG-2384, SEC-112, SUP-879. Rationale and threat model are captured in the design doc linked from the Linear ticket.

release_notes: Add optional KMS consumption governor and residency-aware audit-cohort linking. Feature is opt-in via cluster config and exposes a backfill tool to annotate historical KMS events. Admins should review governor defaults before enabling hard limits. See docs/ops/kms-governor.md for configuration and rollout guidance.
